scope: Proposition 6.2 (Thin-strip estimate) of the manuscript “Endpoint convergence for the planar Schrodinger equation” (preprints/Endpoint-convergence-for-the-planar-Schrodinger-equation-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 080 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 68d6affc8c3cc3bc), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 52. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let U be a finite two-dimensional packet array of the form (2.2), with the fixed profile and phase-space bounds stated there. Suppose all frequency labels lie within distance C/L of an affine line in frequency space. Let µ be supported in a spatial square of side O(L2) and in |t| ≤ L2, and suppose µ(Br) ≤ mr2 for every ball with arbitrary center and every r ≥ 1. Then, with the exponent p0 of Proposition 6.1, µ{|U| ≥ gL−4/3 } ≤ CmL4 g−p0 ∥c∥p0 2 , g > 0. (6.19) The constant depends only on the fixed bounds, including the strip width constant. No sparsity hypothesis is required.
